title: Interactive failover simulator and token-latency SLI walkthrough
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Build an interactive simulation and dashboard that lets SREs and platform engineers rehearse multi-region failover scenarios while observing token-level latency SLIs and circuit-breaker behavior. This ticket covers the instrumentation spec, a lightweight simulation harness, dashboard design, and a runbook walkthrough for on-call use.

Context: We currently have token-level SLI ingest and several dashboards, but it's hard to reproduce realistic multi-region degradations and validate that circuit parameters (hysteresis, admission thresholds, fallback routing) do what we expect at token granularity. This causes risk during real incidents and makes tuning conservative. An interactive simulator paired with reproducible traces will let us iterate on SLO configs, shed policies, and rollout strategies without impacting production.

Goals: 
1) Provide a simulator that can replay sampled token traces across regions and inject controlled faults (eg. GPU slowdowns, KV cache misses, network egress spikes).
2) Surface token-level SLIs (p50/p95/p99 per request-token, admit vs decode latencies) and correlated circuit states in a single dashboard.
3) Create a step-by-step runbook and guided walkthrough for on-call to exercise failover and validate rollbacks.
4) Define acceptance criteria and automated smoke tests for the simulator and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can replay a 10k-token synthetic trace across two regions with configurable latency perturbations
Dashboard shows token-level p50/p95/p99 and token-admit vs decode split for each region and global fanout
Circuit state and recent transitions are visible and linked to histogram of requests that triggered state change
Runbook contains 6 reproducible steps and a checklist; tested in canary environment by on-call
End-to-end test validates that a simulated 30% GPU slowdown in region A triggers planned fallback to region B within configured SLO window
implementation_notes: Sampling: use existing per-token sampling pipeline but add a dev flag to enable full-trace replay for CI/canary
Simulator harness: Python service that consumes prerecorded traces from artifact store and emits to the same telemetry pipeline with an attribute 'sim.run_id'
Trace artifacts: store compressed traces in s3://redwood-sim-artifacts/ with metadata (model, seq_len_distribution, kv_hit_rate)
Telemetry tagging: add fields 'sim.injected_fault', 'simregion', and 'sim_priority' to correlate with production data
Dashboard: Grafana dashboard with four main panels (token latency waterfall, admit vs decode split, circuit state timeline, SLO burnup by region)
Back-compat: simulator must not change production sampling defaults; simulator writes to a dev telemetry topic unless explicitly gated
Privacy: scrub tenant identifiers from saved traces; keep a mapping table in internal vault for authorized replay
dashboard_panels: Regional token-latency heatmap (seq length buckets vs p95/p99) with sim overlay
Admit vs decode latency stacked bar per region with per-token percentiles
Probabilistic circuit state timeline with recent transition events and cause tags
SLO burnup panel showing per-region SLO error budget consumption for token-p99
Sim control panel: sliders to inject latency multiplier, kv-miss-rate, and ingress spike for selected region
Trace-linked panel: recent simulated trace IDs with links to raw trace artifacts and request sample snapshots
telemetry_changes: Emit 'token_phase' tag with values admit|decode|postprocess for clearer breakdown
Add boolean 'is_simulation' to events so dashboards can toggle simulated vs production views
Increase digest retention for token latency histograms for simulation namespaces to 90 days
Add a lightweight SLI exporter to compute token-level p99s grouped by region and model and publish to metrics store
rollout_plan: Week 1: instrument telemetry changes behind feature flag; land simulator basic harness in staging
Week 2: build Grafana panels and link to staging telemetry; review with SRE and on-call lead
Week 3: run a controlled rehearsal with 2x engineers and 1 on-call in staging; iterate on visualizations
Week 4: soft-launch in canary with non-critical tenant traces (scrubbed); run acceptance tests
Post-launch: schedule a 1-hour runbook training session with SRE rotation and Collect feedback for dashboard UX
tests: Unit tests for simulator input parsing and event emission
Integration test that replays a saved trace and asserts SLI metrics change as expected in the metrics store
Chaos test harness that validates fallback occurs when region latency exceeds configured threshold
On-call tabletop exercise recorded and stored as a playbook artifact
